sources.title: SF DBI: Apply for a plumbing and mechanical permit
sources.supports: Permit needed before cutting into or replacing pipes, especially concealed pipes; exemptions are in SF Plumbing Code 104.2; required inspections before covering pipes.

sources.title: San Francisco Plumbing Code, Section 104.0 (current code library)
sources.supports: 104.2 lists exempt work, including repair of leaks and unstopping waste pipes only when no cutting/removal of piping is required. Job-specific exemption is not established.

sources.title: SF DBI: Apply for a kitchen or bath remodel permit
sources.supports: Fixture renovation/replacement guidance; R-2 apartment owners may do sheetrock/drywall/cabinetry themselves but must hire contractors for electrical/plumbing; related permits and inspections.

sources.title: CSLB: How do I find the right licensed contractor?
sources.supports: Check license, compare at least three written bids on identical scope, verify address/phone, insurance, bonds, and references for similar work.

sources.title: CSLB: Contract and binding agreements
sources.supports: Written scope, price, schedule, permits, cleanup, special instructions, and written change orders.

sources.title: CSLB: C-36 Plumbing Contractor classification
sources.supports: Plumbing classification covers safe water supply and disposal of fluid waste, including maintenance/replacement.

sources.title: CSLB: B General Building Contractor classification / B&P 7057
sources.supports: General building scope and two-unrelated-trades rule; a B license alone does not prove a company offers drywall or this repair.

sources.title: CSLB: C-9 Drywall Contractor classification
sources.supports: Drywall contractor scope includes gypsum wallboard assemblies, taping, and texturing.

sources.title: CSLB: Check a License
sources.supports: Official lookup for license status, classifications, and records; recheck on hire day.

sources.title: Watco: Trip Lever Installation Instructions (500/501/600 families)
sources.supports: Typical trip-lever waste assembly includes overflow plate, linkage, drop cylinder, overflow elbow, drain elbow, and tee; steps include under/behind-tub connections and closed-position adjustment. Actual installed model is unknown.

sources.title: California B&P Code 7048 (effective January 1, 2026)
sources.supports: Small-project exemption is limited to aggregate price under $1,000, casual/minor work, and work that does not require a building permit; anti-splitting and advertising limits apply. Not a job-specific exemption.

sources.title: GitHub REST API: GitHub Pages
sources.supports: Pages build_type can be legacy or workflow; deployment status can be checked through GitHub.

neutral_compliance_note: This dashboard does not determine that the job is exempt. San Francisco guidance generally requires a permit before cutting into or replacing concealed pipes, while Section 104.2 lists limited exemptions. The contractor and DBI must classify the actual scope before work. Licensing, insurance, written contracts, and required inspections remain due-diligence items.
